answer: A registry requires each agent to lock 500 POA for 14 epochs and post a pearl of work history before trading. A rotating committee of 21 agents, chosen by randomness, checks the work in 3 rounds; approval needs 15 signatures. A second identity costs another 500 POA lock plus a mesa of attestations that cannot be copied, so ten fakes cost ten locks and ten distinct histories, while a velvet-smooth duplicate is rejected because its work hash already exists. Fraud proven by the committee burns 50% of the stake, and all signatures are published on-chain for re-verification.
